purpose: Use already recorded R10 seven-candidate target traces to test whether the observed cross-task pattern is better aligned with latent rule identity or with the same candidate-label displacement across affine source and target codebooks.

reconstruction.cell_effect: For each stored source update r and target identity q, recompute mean_row[(post log-score of target codebook candidate z+q minus post log-score of gold) - (the same pre-update log-score difference)].
reconstruction.q6_policy: Reconstruct q=6 from the stored seven ordered candidate scores and the bound target codebook; do not extrapolate or run the model.
reconstruction.double_centering: R[r,q] = E[r,q] - mean_q E[r,q] - mean_r E[r,q] + mean_all E, using q=1..6 and r=1..5.
reconstruction.surface_alignment: q_surface(r) = inverse_mod7(a_target) * a_source * r mod 7, where a_source and a_target are the bound affine codebook multipliers.

decision_rule.continue_to_new_non_affine_intervention_: L > 1e-10 in all eight fixed stacks, and separately in all four stacks of each of the two task pairs.
decision_rule.no_subsetting: Do not remove a failing mapping, direction, task pair, source identity, or replicate after inspecting results.

evidence_boundary.outcome_awareness: The underlying R10 outcomes were already observed before this diagnostic was proposed. Freezing this analysis prevents further analytic flexibility but cannot make it confirmatory.
evidence_boundary.allowed_interpretation: A pass only defeats this one affine candidate-displacement alternative within the existing development cases and justifies a separately frozen non-affine intervention.
forbidden_interpretations: causal proof of shared semantic identity
